claim: On 2022-07-27 Global Accelerator added dual-stack accelerators: an IPv4 accelerator gets two static IPv4 addresses, and a dual-stack accelerator gets four addresses, two static IPv4 and two static IPv6.
question: When did Global Accelerator add dual-stack accelerators, and how many addresses do they get?

values.display: a total of four addresses: two static IPv4 addresses and two static IPv6 addresses

qualifiers.scope: AWS Global Accelerator static IP addresses
qualifiers.condition: the What's New announcement is dated 2022-07-28

evidence.quote: | Updates for dual-stack accelerators | Global Accelerator now supports dual-stack accelerators. For IPv4, Global Accelerator provides two static IPv4 addresses. For dual-stack, Global Accelerator provides a total of four addresses: two static IPv4 addresses and two static IPv6 addresses. For more information, see [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/what-is-global-accelerator.html](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/what-is-global-accelerator.html). | July 27, 2022 |

note: d135. Matches the hypothesis 2022-07 of the brief.

claim: On 2023-08-22 Global Accelerator added client IP address preservation for Network Load Balancers with security groups; today three standard-accelerator endpoint types can preserve the client IP address: Application Load Balancers, Amazon EC2 instances, and Network Load Balancers with security groups.
question: When did Global Accelerator add client IP address preservation for Network Load Balancers, and which endpoint types support it now?

values.display: Application Load Balancers, Amazon EC2 instances, and Network Load Balancers with security groups

qualifiers.scope: AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerators, client IP address preservation
qualifiers.condition: Network Load Balancers need security groups; Elastic IP addresses are not supported

evidence.quote: | Adds support for client IP address preservation for Network Load Balancers | Global Accelerator now supports enabling client IP address preservation for Network Load Balancers with security groups. There are three types of endpoints for standard accelerators that can preserve the source IP address of the client in incoming packets: Application Load Balancers, Amazon EC2 instances, and Network Load Balancers with security groups.
